final.memo:
We maintain our position in The Walt Disney Company as we move into the implementation phase of the governance agreement reached in September 2022 [D07]. The appointment of Carolyn Everson to the board provides the necessary internal oversight to hold management accountable to their operational targets [D03]. With the company's announcement of a $5.5 billion cost savings program, the primary catalyst has shifted from initial constructivist engagement to the execution of these efficiency mandates [D03].

While the market continues to harbor concerns regarding secular network erosion and the cash intensity of the direct-to-consumer business—which reported an operating loss of approximately $1.1 billion in the latest quarter—our thesis focuses on the durability of the parks franchise and the potential for improved capital allocation [D01, D03, D05]. We must distinguish between temporary margin pressure and structural impairment; the current cost-action plan is a concrete step toward the latter [D03, D05].

We remain disciplined in our view that selling before the results of this management plan are evidenced would forfeit the upside of our prior engagement [D05]. Our holding reflects the constraints of the existing standstill agreement and our commitment to seeing the agreed-upon strategic adjustments through to realization [D03, D07].
